This also throws, which you've failed to catch.

To handle these exceptions, I had to do serious code refactoring here.

What I did was:
1. API of the functions in this file only accept DateFormat enum and not TZs, this guarantees the code outside of this file (that uses these functions) will not try to retrieve TZ, so it does not need to handle exceptions.
2. Byproduct of #1 - *Tz functions not needed and were deleted.
3. details::toISO8061ExtendedStr accept offset in minutes and not TZ, this what it needs really, but also allows to limit number of places calling locate_zone/current_zone functions.
4. This function was changed to return offset and not TZ, this allows to call locate_zone/current_zone and handle exception only here, and fall back to UTC (offset 0).

This also required refactoring unit tests, in particular, most of this logic is not exposed directly outside of this cpp, so to test it without exposure, I introduced a new time_utils_internal.hpp which is supposed to be used only in tests.
All of that sounds reasonable to me.  Reviewing in a moment.

I've fixed the merge conflict here, and resolved the merge conflict with my patch.  We're writing a bunch of code that (unless I'm mistaken) is already handled in zoned_time, we just need to update some of our types to handle that correctly.  Was that considered?

@ifelmail@gmail.com have you had a chance to look at the change?

My main concern about your implementation - you got rid of DateFormat enum and accept const std::chrono::time_zone* in "getDateTimeUint*" functions, developers who need to call one of these function with non default TZ may use `std::chrono::current_zone()` at the call site without properly handling exceptions. Yes, this might be caught on review, but this introduces human factor, so it might be safer to keep the DateFormat enum in place, use "DateFormat::LocalTimezone" as default and keep TZ retrieval logic in one place with the error handing. Otherwise LGTM.

WDYT?
Sorry, it was a long holiday in the UK and I was AFK. Looked now.

> My main concern about your implementation - you got rid of DateFormat enum

To be clear, I did this so we could unit test it across multiple timezones.  The UTC/localtime enum didn't let us unit test across all timezones, and didn't give us the ability to test localtime at all, because we don't know what timezone the system running the unit tests is in.

> and accept const std::chrono::time_zone* in "getDateTimeUint*" functions, developers who need to call one of these function with non default TZ may use `std::chrono::current_zone()` at the call site without properly handling exceptions.

While I agree it's a potential for issues, I don't have control of the std library implementation.

> Yes, this might be caught on review, but this introduces human factor, so it might be safer to keep the DateFormat enum in place, use "DateFormat::LocalTimezone" as default and keep TZ retrieval logic in one place with the error handing. Otherwise LGTM.

What if we changed that argument to just passing in a timezone string that's then looked up internally?  That way we can unit test across a bunch of timezones, while still keeping the current_zone() call internal to the implementation?

Under the assumption that that would improve things, I've updated the patch above with that behavior.  PTAL and integrate into your patch if you think it's correct.  I believe the only thing left to do is to update unit tests to test the range of all timezones instead of just UTC.
